proposal.title: Alternator Premature Failure
proposal.description: The complete reviewed 226-row MPV manufacturer-communication inventory contains battery testing and charging guidance but no exact Mazda record establishing premature alternator failure from exhaust heat across 1990-2006. The frozen record has no usable citation, spans two MPV generations and provides no source for the stored 140-owner total. Charging warnings or a discharged battery do not by themselves identify the alternator.
proposal.solution: Load-test the battery and inspect charging voltage, voltage drop, grounds, fuses, belt drive, tensioner, wiring and parasitic draw before condemning the alternator. If the vehicle is losing electrical power while driving, move it to a safe location and arrange diagnosis. Do not buy an alternator, heat shield, battery, belt or tensioner from this page; the failed component, heat mechanism and exact fitment have not been established.
symptoms: low charging voltage confirmed by testing
electrical systems weakening while the engine is running

before.title: Rear Coil Spring Corrosion and Fracture
before.description: The MPV's rear coil springs corrode and fracture in rust-belt states, typically breaking at the bottom coil. A broken spring causes the rear of the vehicle to sag on one side and can puncture a tire if the broken end shifts. The springs lose their protective coating from road salt and moisture, and the tightly wound lower coils trap debris that accelerates corrosion.
before.solution: Replace both rear coil springs as a pair ($100-$200 for a pair of aftermarket springs). Never replace just one side. MOOG and Monroe are reliable aftermarket options. Inspect the spring perches and shock absorbers during replacement. Spray new springs with rubberized undercoating after installation. An annual undercoating application helps prevent recurrence in rust-belt climates.
symptoms: Vehicle leans to one side in rear
Rear ride height lower than normal
Tire damage from broken spring end

citations.title: YouTube Repair Video on Replacing Rear Coil Springs on Mazda MPV

communityRecommendations.content: Check your rear springs every spring (pun intended) — look for rust and cracks on the lower coils. A broken spring can puncture your tire on the highway. MOOG replacements are $50 each and a 1-hour job per side.

proposal.title: Rear Coil Spring Corrosion and Fracture
proposal.description: The complete reviewed MPV communication and recall inventory contains no exact Mazda record establishing rear coil-spring corrosion and fracture across 2000-2006. The frozen page cites a fabricated video identifier and imports a corrosion/tire-puncture mechanism that NHTSA investigations document for other vehicles, not the MPV. No exact source supports mandatory paired replacement, named aftermarket brands or annual undercoating.
proposal.solution: If the rear sits unevenly, a spring is visibly fractured, or metal is near a tire, stop and have both rear suspension sides inspected for spring damage, perch corrosion, tire contact, dampers and attachment-point damage. Follow the Mazda workshop procedure and confirm the exact spring specification before repair. Do not buy coil springs, shocks, undercoating or mounting hardware from this page; the defect, damage and vehicle fitment have not been established.
symptoms: visible broken or displaced spring material
metal contact near a rear tire requiring immediate inspection

proposal.title: Power Sliding Door Malfunction
proposal.description: Mazda communications document several distinct MPV sliding-door conditions: an upper roller concern on 2000-2001 vehicles, service guidance for inoperative or improper power-door operation on 2002-2005 vehicles, and a 2002-2006 condition where a power door re-opens after starting to close and latch. Those records do not establish one recurring motor/cable/latch failure across the frozen 2000-2007 scope, and no reviewed source supports the stored 160-owner total.
proposal.solution: Identify the exact door, model year, manual-versus-power equipment and failure mode. Inspect tracks, rollers, latches, switches, wiring, drive module, motor and cable only as the applicable Mazda procedure directs; do not defeat pinch protection or force a door that will not latch. Do not buy a motor, cable, latch, roller, drive module or lubricant from this page; the applicable communication, failed component and fitment must be confirmed first.
symptoms: power sliding door inoperative or operating improperly
door that re-opens after starting to close and latch
upper roller or track concern requiring inspection

proposal.title: Automatic Transmission Shudder and Failure
proposal.description: Mazda MSP03 / communication 10023158 covers certain 2003-2004 MPVs built from April 1, 2003 through January 26, 2004 with intermittent shift shock during warm-up, usually on 1-2 or 2-3 upshifts or a 3-2 part-throttle downshift. Mazda attributes most covered cases to TCM software calibration. That narrow program does not establish the frozen 2000-2007 torque-converter-shudder and eventual internal-failure identity, and no reviewed source supports the stored 180-owner total.
proposal.solution: Record the exact shift, temperature, load, speed and stored codes, then verify VIN/build applicability to MSP03 before mechanical repair. Diagnose fluid condition and level, controls, software calibration, engine inputs, torque converter and internal transmission separately. Mazda SA-029/26 says to follow the vehicle-specific schedule and discourages unprescribed fluid flushing. Do not buy fluid, a torque converter, valve body, solenoid, rebuild or transmission from this page; the failure path and fitment have not been established.
symptoms: intermittent 1-2 or 2-3 shift shock during warm-up on the MSP03 population
3-2 part-throttle downshift shock on the MSP03 population
other shudder, slip or delay requiring separate diagnosis

before.title: Automatic Transmission Slipping and Harsh Shifting
before.description: The second-generation MPV's 5-speed automatic transmission (shared with Ford) develops slipping, harsh shifts, and delayed engagement between 80,000-120,000 miles. The torque converter lock-up clutch wears, and the valve body solenoids stick. The transmission fluid often shows signs of degradation (dark color, burnt smell) well before problems are felt. Towing or heavy passenger loads accelerate wear.
before.solution: Change transmission fluid and filter every 30,000 miles with Mercon V ATF. A fluid change can temporarily improve mild slipping. If the torque converter shudder is present, a Mercon LV fluid change may help. Failed transmissions require rebuild ($1,800-$3,000) or replacement with a remanufactured unit ($2,000-$3,500). Jasper and Certified Transmission offer remanufactured units with warranties.
symptoms: Delayed engagement from Park to Drive
Check engine light with trans codes

communityRecommendations.content: Change the trans fluid every 30k miles — don't listen to the "lifetime fluid" myth. Drain-and-fill only (NOT a full flush) with Mercon V. The MPV trans is Ford-sourced and needs regular fluid changes to survive.
Transmission flush kit for complete fluid exchange to address shudder
Full synthetic ATF designed to reduce shudder in automatic transmissions

proposal.title: Automatic Transmission Slipping and Harsh Shifting
proposal.description: The reviewed inventory does not establish a uniform 5-speed transmission slipping, torque-converter-clutch wear and stuck-solenoid defect across every 2000-2006 MPV or the frozen 80,000-120,000-mile window. The exact MSP03 record is limited to certain 2003-2004 vehicles with intermittent warm-up shift shock caused in most cases by TCM calibration. Communication 10206002 describes cooler-line power flushing only before installation of an overhauled or replacement transmission, not routine preventive flushing.
proposal.solution: Preserve codes and document the exact shift event before service. Verify fluid level and condition using the year-specific Mazda procedure, check MSP03 VIN/build applicability, and diagnose software, controls, converter and internal hydraulics separately. Do not substitute generic Mercon advice or routine flush intervals for the owner/workshop schedule. Do not buy fluid, a filter, additive, converter, valve body, solenoid, rebuild or transmission from this page; specification, cause and fitment have not been established.
symptoms: slipping or delayed engagement requiring measured diagnosis
harsh shift requiring code and calibration checks
warm-up shift shock on the defined MSP03 population
